coremath_2_2-093.typed: A driver in a Kenyan vehicle looks into the rear-view mirror and sees a lorry approaching from behind. The driver observes that the lorry's right headlight appears on the right-hand side of the mirror image when the lorry is directly aligned behind the vehicle. This raises questions about how plane mirrors form images and why images sometimes appear laterally inverted.For teaching lateral inversion, use the reversed word AMBULANCE on the front of an ambulance or a reversed letter F. These provide clearer examples of apparent left-right reversal. | Accept the scientific correction  but retain the lorry phenomenon as a real-life introduction to reflection. Teach lateral inversion separately using the ambulance example.
